text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tories' megacity bill now law: Opponents beat drums, blow whistles outside legislature, call 'shame' from galleries.
- Thomas acquires control of Raptors: Plans to end feud with Leafs.
- Tobacco companies fighting back: Dingwall's concessions used in support of legal challenge to new bill.
- Chirac calls election 10 months early: French President defends move, says new spirit needed to face challenges ahead.
- Flood waters roll toward Manitoba: Crest of swollen Red River moves north after devastating North Dakota, Minnesota.
- Spending spree sparks economy: Consumer and business trade jumps 3 percent in February, far beyond predictions.
- Sears to spend $C300 million on face lift: Injection comes after years of restraint.
- Japan eyes Canada's budget balancing act.
- The rate game has its price: Peace of mind in 5-year mortgage may bring extra cost, study.
- US$600-million Imasco deal seen: Shared jump on news that CKE Restaurants wants to buy the Hardee's trademark and some 700 Imasco-owned restaurants for between US$500 million and US$600 million.
